statement: Yamaha's 2020 service manual (shared with the YZ125) lists the YZ125X as model YZ125XL for the USA, Canada and Australia, model code B1B5 (USA, Canada) and B1B6 (Australia); 2020 was its first year.

The 2020 YZ125X uses the YZ125's 125 cc 54.0 x 54.5 mm reed-valve two-stroke but with a bigger combustion chamber: 10.0-10.2 cc against 8.30-8.50 cc on the YZ125, lowering compression to 7.4-8.8:1 (YZ125 8.6-10.7:1). Reeds 0.470 mm thick, stopper height 8.2-8.6 mm.

Carbureted with a Mikuni TMX38SS. The manual's US/Canada jetting: I.D. 1C37 51, main jet #430, needle 6BFY43-74 clip 3, cutaway 4, pilot jet #40, pilot air screw 2-1/4 turns out, valve seat 3.8 mm, starter jet #80, fuel level 9.5-10.5 mm. CDI ignition with a digital advancer, timing 0.50 mm BTDC; no map switch.
notes: The 2020 manual's jetting table is not split by model; the YZ125X-only 2021 manual (B1B-2819U-10) lists the identical #430/6BFY43-74-3/#40/2-1/4 setting, so it applies to the X.

statement: Engine controls on the 2020 YZ125X are a CDI with digital advancer and the mechanical YPVS power valve; Yamaha lists no handlebar map switch or selectable ignition map.

KYB 48 mm inner-tube coil fork, 300 mm travel, standard spring 4.10 N/mm, 425 cc of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 per leg on the YZ125X (510 cc on the YZ125), damper oil level 145-148 mm; standard rebound 11 clicks out, compression 15 clicks out (of 20); fork tubes 5 mm above the top clamp.

KYB shock, 315 mm wheel travel (131.5 mm shaft), standard spring 46 N/mm (red, 260 mm free length) set to a 254 mm fitting length on the X (252 mm YZ125), preload range 1.5-18 mm; standard rebound 12-15 clicks out, low-speed compression 12-15 clicks out, high-speed compression 1-5/8 +/- 1/6 turns out; 1,000 kPa nitrogen.
Yamaha's manual gives the X's standard fork rebound as 11 clicks out; one magazine test listed 9 as stock and also ran 4.1 N/mm fork and 46 N/mm shock springs with 105 mm race sag.
notes: Kept side by side: the OSM figure is the authoritative standard.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2020 Yamaha YZ125X cross-country

statement: Six-speed close-ratio box: primary 3.368 (64/19), gears 2.385, 1.933, 1.588, 1.353, 1.200, 1.095; final drive 50/13 (3.846) on the X versus 48/13 on the YZ125. Optional rear sprockets 47-52 teeth; drive chain D.I.D 520MXV5 O-ring, 114 links.
Wet multi-plate clutch with 8 friction plates (2.90-3.10 mm, limit 2.80) and 7 steel plates, five springs of 40.10 mm free length (limit 38.10); inner-push cam release; kick-and-mesh kickstarter.

topic: YZ125X engine differences from the YZ125 (2020-2022)
statement: Versus the YZ125 the first-generation X lowers compression partly by raising the spark plug 3 mm, uses stiffer power-valve springs and a reshaped valve so the YPVS starts opening at 8,000 rpm (YZ 7,500) and is fully open at 10,250 rpm (YZ 9,500), lowers the exhaust port 0.5 mm, and advances ignition about 5 degrees low to mid while retarding it slightly mid to top.
notes: Magazine report of the 2020 changes; Yamaha manuals for 2021 and 2022 list the same compression, jetting and gearing, so the same engine spec is assumed.

statement: The first-generation YZ125X has a milder, more tractable powerband than the YZ125, deliberately giving up some peak for control in tight, slow going.

statement: Yamaha introduced the 2023 YZ125X with a completely redesigned 125 two-stroke (more power and usability than the 2022), revised YPVS timing, a model-specific 3D-map digital CDI, a new Keihin PWK38S carburetor with power jet, a revised close-ratio six-speed with wider gear teeth, revised suspension damping, new brakes, new YZ styling and new ergonomics.
Yamaha describes the 2023 YZ125X engine as an increase in power and usability over the 2022 model, with broad, usable delivery aimed at cross-country and enduro racing.
The 2023 YZ125X uses its own digital CDI with 3D-map ignition timing (different from the YZ125 motocrosser) plus revised YPVS timing for low-mid tractability.
Yamaha describes the 2027 YZ125X engine as giving strong acceleration and exciting mid-to-high rpm power with good usability.

For 2027 Yamaha lists a Keihin PWK38S carburetor with power jet and throttle position sensor, a 3D-map CDI and a model-specific digital CDI unit compared with the YZ125, plus optimized YPVS settings; there are no selectable maps.
Yamaha specifies a 48 mm Speed Sensitive System KYB fork and a fully adjustable KYB shock with Kashima-coated internals, both with a cross-country-focused setup.

Testers found the second-generation X surprisingly torquey for a 125: it can lug a taller gear without an immediate downshift yet still likes to rev, and it has less engine braking than the motocross bike, which helps carry momentum.
notes: Test of the 2024; Yamaha manuals list identical engine/carb/gearbox specs 2023-2027.

statement: Common complaints on the 2023-on X: no electric start and the motocross-size 7.0 L (1.8 gal) tank, which limits range on long loops; heavier or faster riders may want the cross-country valving stiffened for high-speed terrain.
notes: Tank size from Yamaha manuals 2023-2027.

statement: The KYB fork and shock run softer settings than the YZ125 and absorb repeated rock, root and braking-bump hits better, with slower rebound that uses all the travel.
Yamaha's 2020 service manual (shared with the YZ250) lists the YZ250X as model YZ250XL for the USA, Canada and Australia, model code BF1H (USA, Canada) and BF1K (Australia).

249 cc 66.4 x 72.0 mm reed-valve two-stroke; the X's combustion chamber is 23.45-23.75 cc against 21.35-21.65 cc on the YZ250, giving 7.9-9.4:1 compression (YZ250 8.9-10.6:1). Reeds 0.420 mm, stopper height 10.3-10.7 mm; Keihin PWK38S carburetor.

Carbureted Keihin PWK38S, US/Canada jetting: I.D. 1P87 50, main #178, main air jet #200, needle N3EW clip 2, needle jet 2.9, cutaway #7, pilot #50, air screw 1-1/4 turns, valve seat 3.8 mm, starter #85, power jet #50, float arm height 6.5 mm. CDI ignition, YPVS governor, no map switch.
notes: Table is not split by model; the 2021 and 2022 YZ250X manuals list the same jetting.

statement: KYB 48 mm coil fork, 300 mm travel, standard spring 4.30 N/mm (same as YZ250), 515 cc S1 oil per leg, damper oil level 145-148 mm; standard rebound 10 clicks out, compression 13 out (of 20).

KYB shock, 315 mm travel, standard spring 48 N/mm (black, 260 mm free length) at a 248 mm fitting length, preload range 1.5-18 mm; standard rebound 10-13 clicks out, low-speed compression 11-14 out, high-speed 1-5/8 +/- 1/6 turns out.

Five-speed: primary 3.000 (63/21); X ratios 1.929, 1.533, 1.313, 1.050, 0.840 (YZ250: 3rd 1.278, 4th 1.091, 5th 0.952); final 50/14 (3.571); optional sprockets 13-14 front and 47-52 rear; D.I.D 520VM2 chain, 114 links.
8 friction plates (2.90-3.10 mm), 7 steel plates and six clutch springs of 44.00 mm free length on the X (50.00 mm on the YZ250) for a lighter pull; ratchet kickstarter.

statement: The X is milder and more tractable than the YZ250, with a perky low-to-mid pull suited to rocky, tight terrain that lets riders go faster with less hesitation, but it is not a motocross start-line powerband.

Range got shorter: Yamaha's manuals show the YZ250X tank cut from 8.0 L (2.1 gal) in 2022 to 7.0 L (1.8 gal) from 2023 on; testers already rated the 8.0 L tank too small for long off-road loops.

notes: Magazine summary of Yamaha information.

source.name: Dirt Rider - 2022 Yamaha enduro motorcycles first look

statement: Testers found the 2022 engine stronger across the range, especially mid to top where it revs more freely, so gears can be held longer.
notes: European test of the 2022; US manuals show 2023-2024 engine specs unchanged.

statement: Stalling and awkward hot restarts remain a WR250F trait though better than earlier models; it stalls more readily than a two-stroke in technical going, and a softer map reduces stalling.
With only about 0.95 L of engine oil (dry fill), testers advise frequent oil changes on the WR250F.
notes: Yamaha manuals list 0.95 L disassembled capacity.

topic: WR250F market differences in tuning access
statement: European-market 2022 WR250Fs were tested with the Power Tuner smartphone app and a handlebar switch between full and softer maps; the US 2022-2024 manuals list neither, only the optional handheld GYTR Power Tuner.
The 2027 WR250F returns unchanged with a US MSRP of $9,199.

statement: The 2022 WR450F returned mechanically unchanged after its 2021 update, with new radiator-shroud graphics and a $100 price rise to $9,899.

source.name: Dirt Rider - 2022 Yamaha enduro motorcycles first look

topic: WR450F traction control via Power Tuner
statement: Yamaha's WR450F has a three-level traction control (HIGH, LOW, OFF) enabled through the Power Tuner app, which reads wheel slip into the ECU; ECU settings are tailored for trail and enduro.
notes: 2025 features page; the 2026 US manual lists identical specs and the same app/CCU and mode switch.

statement: Yamaha says the WR450F's 450 cc DOHC engine is light and compact with strong pulling power, and its high rev limit helps over-rev for a broad power character.
Yamaha lists a compact disc-spring clutch whose primary gear and basket are one steel unit, and a wide-ratio five-speed gearbox for off-road use.
Fully adjustable KYB coil fork with speed-sensitive damping and a new hand-operated compression clicker for tool-free changes.
Aluminum bilateral beam frame of more than ten welded components with WR450F-specific engine mounts.

Testers found the 2025 WR450F fast and willing to rev, with low first gear for crawling and enough torque in second and third to pull out of corners with little clutch; the mellow handlebar map tames it for slippery going.
notes: Australian test of a 2025; the 2026 US manual lists identical specs.

source.name: Australasian Dirt Bike - Enduro test: 2025 Yamaha WR450F

statement: The flameout problem of older WRs is mostly gone, though bogging it in too high a gear can still make it sputter; the suspension can feel a little firm at slow pace and the 955 mm seat is tall.

source.name: Australasian Dirt Bike - Enduro test: 2025 Yamaha WR450F

statement: Start on the mellow map (blue light) in slick conditions and switch to full power once the ground dries; back off compression damping for a softer ride at slow pace.

source.name: Australasian Dirt Bike - Enduro test: 2025 Yamaha WR450F

statement: For 2027 the WR450F takes the latest YZ450F engine tuned for low and midrange, with a revised intake port, new cam timing and a heavier AC magneto rotor to smooth low-rpm delivery and resist stalling, plus a new air filter assembly, lighter throttle and quieter resonator.
notes: Magazine summary of Yamaha information.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2027 Yamaha WR450F first look

statement: The Power Tuner app on the 2027 WR450F offers three-level traction control, a lap timer, data logging, suspension tuning guides and an owner-set ECU lock; an optional GYTR Competition ECU kit adds engine tuning and launch control for closed-course use.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2027 Yamaha WR450F first look

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2027 Yamaha WR450F first look

statement: New bilateral beam frame shared with the 2027 YZ450F with WR engine brackets; rake up one degree to 27 deg and trail from 4.3 to 4.8 in, wheelbase unchanged at 57.9 in; claimed wet weight down 2 lb to 256 lb; rear disc 220 mm (was 240); Dunlop Geomax AT82 tires; MSRP $10,499.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2027 Yamaha WR450F first look

statement: Low-rpm stalling on the previous WR450F was a target of the 2027 update: Yamaha fitted more magneto inertia and revised cam timing to resist stalling.
notes: Inferred from the stated purpose of the changes, not from a failure report.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2027 Yamaha WR450F first look

statement: On a magazine in-house dyno the YZ250FX of this generation made 37.9 hp at 12,100 rpm and 18.3 lb-ft at 8,800 rpm.
notes: Measured on a 2022; the 2022 and 2023 US manuals list identical specifications.

source.name: Dirt Rider - Yamaha YZ250FX dyno test 2022

statement: Testers found exceptional low-end torque for a 250F that lets it lug and chug, a strong mid-range and a top end competitive with the highest-revving 250s; gears 3-6 pull better than before so first and second are rarely needed.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - First impression: 2022 Yamaha YZ250FX

statement: The stock fork feels firm early in the stroke, riding high and resisting bottoming without the usual supple KYB feel, while the shock is on the soft side, leaving the bike unbalanced front to rear until the clickers are reset.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - First impression: 2022 Yamaha YZ250FX

statement: Softening the fork clickers and adding high-speed compression to the shock balanced the 2022 FX; the tester was comfortable racing it close to stock after that.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - First impression: 2022 Yamaha YZ250FX

statement: For 2027 the YZ450FX adopts the updated YZ450F design with adjusted cam timing for low-to-mid usability and a new AC magneto rotor for smoother low-rpm torque on tight trails.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test - First look: 2027 Yamaha YZ450FX

statement: New hydraulic clutch with about 15% less lever pull than the 2026 YZ450F cable clutch, and a 51-tooth rear sprocket (was 50) to need less precise throttle control.
notes: Sprocket confirmed by the 2027 US OSM (51/13).

statement: Yamaha lists a 113 kg wet weight, 7.8 L tank, aluminum bilateral beam frame, tool-free adjustable KYB suspension with 300 mm front and 306 mm rear travel, 270 mm front and 220 mm rear discs and a hydraulic clutch.

source.name: Yamaha Motor New Zealand - 2027 YZ450FX spec sheet

statement: The 2027 YZ450FX keeps the YZ450F's KYB hardware but with settings revised for initial comfort, compliance and mid-stroke response on long cross-country rides.
The 2027 YZ125 and YZ250 carry on with updated Icon Blue colours and graphics only, plus Monster Energy Edition versions; no mechanical changes were announced.
The 2027 YZ450F is also offered as a Monster Energy Edition in team livery; its frame, suspension, clutch and dry-sump layout serve as the base for the all-new 2027 YZ250F.
The 2021 CRF250RX is unchanged from the 2020, which had a major overhaul; MSRP rose $100 to $8,399.

statement: 249.43 cc liquid-cooled four-stroke single inclined 9 deg from vertical, bore x stroke 79.000 x 50.887 mm, compression 13.9:1, throttle body GQA7A, idle 2,000 +/- 100 rpm; valve clearance (cold) intake 0.09 +/- 0.03 mm, exhaust 0.19 +/- 0.03 mm.

topic: CRF250RX engine modes and launch control (2020-2021)
statement: Three PGM-FI engine modes selected by the handlebar button: mode 1 standard, mode 2 smooth (softer response), mode 3 aggressive (sharper response); HRC launch control with three levels (factory level 2) temporarily lowers the rev limit for the start. The 2020 250RX manual lists no torque (traction) control.

Showa coil fork, 305 mm stroke and 268 mm wheel travel; RX standard spring 4.6 N/mm (options 4.4 and 4.8), standard oil 356 cc (range about 306-391 cc), damper oil 243 cc; standard compression 12 clicks and rebound 15 clicks out from fully in (CRF250R 9 and 11).

Pro-Link shock, 317 mm wheel travel; RX standard spring 50 N/mm (options 48 and 52) at a standard preload length of 233.5 mm (228-239 mm range); high-speed compression 2-11/12 to 3-5/12 turns out, low-speed compression 8 clicks, rebound 7-10 clicks; standard race sag 105 mm.

Honda's manual says the RX fork's minimum oil with the standard spring is 306 cc; to cure big-bump harshness turn compression out one click and lower oil in 5 cc steps without going below the minimum; optional softer and stiffer fork and shock springs are listed for rider weight.
Five-speed: primary 3.473, gears 2.230, 1.750, 1.470, 1.227, 1.043; final 3.692 (13/48), optional 49T rear; D.I.D 520 MXV5 O-ring chain, 114 links; wet multi-plate clutch.

topic: 2020 CRF450RX modes, HSTC and launch control
statement: Three PGM-FI modes (1 standard, 2 smooth, 3 aggressive); Torque Control (HSTC) with modes 1, 2 and 3 plus off - mode 1 allows the most rear-wheel slip and mode 3 the least, factory mode 2, inactive on deceleration; HRC launch control with three levels (factory level 2) lowers the rev limit and works with Torque Control off the start, cancelling in third gear.
